scope: local direct-process diagnostic scaling on one macOS ARM64 host; one question and two target records, no network delay injected
toolchain: Rust 1.97.1 pinned by rust-toolchain.toml; release binaries
qualifications: Some diagnostic runs used changing uncommitted source trees. The per-run source_tree_clean flag and source commit distinguish exact-head runs. Every report records release binary hashes. All runs are one-host local diagnostics, not separate-machine acceptance.

storage_256.note: The operating floor is headroom, not reserved bytes. The maximum-run allowance assumes every record uses its bound and is not required before startup.

process_rss_sample.method: ps -axo pid,%cpu,rss,comm; one sample, not a peak

runs.label: 256-exact-head-long-phase-handoff-stall
runs.note: Clean-head run was stopped after 3,861.567 seconds at height zero. All 256 respondents had prepared agreement and one observed all 256 precommits, but READY signatures reached only 1..8 and TERMINAL remained zero. Old-lane connected peers fell to 0..32. A direct sample of node 0 earlier showed 32 staged peers, 496 queued READY deliveries and one READY in flight. This is a handoff delivery/concurrency bottleneck, not proof that the host lacks disk or RAM. No Mac sleep was observed during the run.

runs.label: 256-exact-head-deferred-mesh-bind-failure
runs.note: Clean-head deferred-dial run exited after 515.257 seconds at height zero because eight validators logged "cannot listen for state peers" while preparing their fresh handoff listener. Before exit, the final complete poll found 69 of 246 respondents prepared for agreement and old-lane connected peers 236..255. The harness had allocated listener ports using OS ephemeral binds and released them before the old mesh opened thousands of outbound sockets. A collision is plausible but the transport error did not include an OS cause; this run does not measure READY convergence after deferral.

runs.label: 256-exact-head-fixed-ports-listener-failure
runs.note: Clean-head run with 512 unique listener address/port pairs in 20000..29999 exited after 494.533 seconds at height zero. Many validators logged "cannot listen for state peers" while staging fresh listeners. The libp2p TransportError Display implementation suppressed the underlying I/O cause, so this result disproves the assumption that avoiding this host's ephemeral range alone resolves listener failure, but it does not identify the OS error. The last complete poll saw 57 prepared agreements among 254 respondents and 223..255 old peer links.

runs.label: 256-exact-head-listener-enobufs
runs.note: Clean-head run stopped after 546.529 seconds at height zero when 42 validator logs reported staged-listener failure: No buffer space available (macOS os error 55). Final complete poll had 128 of 225 respondents prepared for agreement and READY range 0..31; old-lane connected range was 232..255. Distinct handoff listener ports were probed in 20000..29999, so this is a host network buffer/resource failure rather than an observed port collision. Cumulative netstat -m after cleanup reported denied network-memory requests, not attributable solely to this run.

runs.label: 256-exact-head-backlog16-enobufs
runs.note: Clean-head 256-process run failed after 540.206 seconds at height zero. Twenty-two validator logs reported macOS No buffer space available (OS error 55) while binding staged listeners despite the 16-slot backlog. Final saved poll had 169 of 204 respondents prepared for agreement, READY 0..5, and no TERMINAL signatures. The release binary hashes match the passing 128-process run, and both used the same listener-port policy. All benchmark validator processes were gone after runner exit.

runs.label: 128-exact-head-sleep-interrupted
runs.note: Clean-head 128-process run was interrupted after 419.657 seconds by a four-second macOS Maintenance Sleep on battery at 10:38:55 local time, despite idle/system caffeinate assertions. All 128 validators rejected further clock reports because UTC drift exceeded two seconds. Before sleep, READY reached 86 of 86 and TERMINAL had begun. This is an invalidated measurement, not a validator or listener-capacity failure; all children were gone after runner exit.

runs.label: 128-exact-head-awake-height2
runs.note: Clean-head 128-process run with display, idle, disk, system and user-activity wake assertions. All 128 validators reached one common height-two head and state; first quorum at 1934.460 seconds and all nodes at 2214.905 seconds. Second-height handoff was slow and staged connectivity sparse for late nodes. The runner could not sample process memory in its sandbox; a separate read-only ps sample at about 09:00 UTC found 128 validators using 4834.8 MiB RSS and 944.2% CPU. All benchmark validator processes were gone after runner exit.
